profile_text.body:
Arm describes itself as a provider of compute platforms behind advanced AI, spanning cloud, edge, and physical AI with consistent software and flexible compute. Per its site, the company's technology powers cloud infrastructure, personal devices, AI-defined vehicles, and robotics, and it says it enables scalable orchestration across cloud and edge environments as AI and compute converge. The Arm AI Portal is described as a single place for developers and agents to discover optimized models, evaluate performance, access deployment workflows, and optimize their own models for Arm. The site also references Arm Create events in Shanghai and Shenzhen that showcased ecosystem work on intelligent applications, and an episode in which Arm's Eddie Ramirez explains why Arm launched the AGI CPU, how agentic AI is reshaping data centers, and why efficiency is becoming a defining metric for the AI era. Arm also points to NVIDIA DGX Spark, built on Arm-based NVIDIA Grace Blackwell technology, for developing, fine-tuning, and running large AI models locally.

The company profile lists Arm as a for-profit public company founded in 1990 and headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom. No products are tracked for it, and no lawsuits are recorded.

The MCP servers listed alongside Arm in the registry are third-party tools rather than Arm offerings, including a data observability server, a hosted Google Calendar server, a contractor search server, a career framework server, a Korean pharmaceutical information server, an ad board, a pharma vendor services server, and a night-fishing game. None is described as an Arm product.
